disagreements.topic: Is the OpenAI stake double counted against the core multiple?
disagreements.positions: Agents 1, 2 and 3 value the core on a cut 'ex-stake' multiple of 22-24x and add $27-28. Agents 4 and 5 run a whole-company P/E leg with no stake beside a core-multiple-plus-stake SOTP leg. Fair values are $520-563 against $518.28 spot.
disagreements.resolution: No double count in any agent. Each ex-stake multiple is derived from spot less the same ~$27 stake: ($518.28 - 27) / NTM EPS $20.74 is about 23.7x. Core EPS is non-GAAP, which excludes the OpenAI equity-method result (FY26 net gains of $6.53B, or $0.67/share, excluded). No agent adds the stake on top of a whole-company multiple. The one inconsistency is agent 5: its headline 23.5x against 22x core implies $36 for the stake while it values it at $28, which is under $3 on the blend. The stake mark itself ($1.1T, midway between the closed $852B post-money and the unclosed ~$1.4T talks, less 25-30%) is the real soft spot. At $852B it is about $21 net; at a closed $1.4T, after about 2% dilution from the $30B raise, about $35. That is ±$7/share, or about 1.4% of price.
disagreements.evidence: 10-K FY26 equity-method note (~25% as-converted) and non-GAAP reconciliation (net gains from OpenAI investments of $6.53B excluded); Yahoo/Bloomberg 2026-09-29 ($30B at ~$1.4T, IPO slipped to 2027)

disagreements.topic: Net debt including finance leases: level and where it is applied
disagreements.positions: All five now use about $33B (cash and short-term investments $76.8B, less debt of $40.3B book or $46.1B face, less $66.6B of finance leases). Agent 1 subtracts it only in its DCF. Agent 2 never subtracts it. Agents 3, 4 and 5 subtract $4-4.5/share from P/E-based SOTP values, and agents 3 and 4 also subtract it in FCF-yield legs.
disagreements.resolution: The level is consistent and correct. The application is not. Subtracting net debt belongs in the DCF (enterprise value) and, partly, in the FCF-yield legs, because finance-lease principal is a financing outflow that FCF never sees. It does not belong in P/E legs, because EPS already includes the interest income on the $76.8B of cash and the interest on debt and finance leases, so the market multiple already reflects the balance sheet. Agents 3, 4 and 5 are therefore about $1.3-3.2/share too low on their blends. The larger lease issue is the flow, not the stock: FY26 finance-lease ROU additions were $24.6B while only $3.1B of finance-lease principal was paid. The roughly $21.5B gap is capex that 'OCF minus additions to PP&E' never deducts, about 1/3 of FY26 FCF of $67.0B. Agent 3's FCF leg misses it (optimistic). Agent 4 instead adds operating-lease spend whose rent is already in OCF (partial double count). Agent 1's DCF cuts margins 2-3pt for it, without showing the arithmetic. Operating leases ($21.9B, plus $329B not yet commenced) correctly stay out of net debt because their rent runs through OCF.
disagreements.evidence: 10-K FY26 balance sheet; Note 10 (debt $40.3B book, $46.1B face, fair value $36.5B); Note 13 lease tables (finance lease liabilities $66.6B; FY26 cash paid: operating leases $6.44B, finance-lease interest $2.55B, finance-lease principal $3.10B; ROU additions: finance $24.6B, operating $4.6B); cash flow statement (OCF $182.9B, PP&E additions $115.9B)
